chunks: Yaḥyā ibn al-Qushayrī from a village called Qīr narrated to me; he said:

Abū Muḥammad had an agent who had taken for himself a room in the house, and with him there was a white servant. The agent desired the servant for himself, but he refused unless he brought him nabīdh. So he contrived to get nabīdh for him, then brought it in to him, while between him and Abū Muḥammad there were three locked doors.

He said: The agent narrated to me, saying: I was alert when suddenly the doors were opening until he himself came and stood at the door of the room. Then he said: O you people, have taqwa of Allah; fear Allah. So when morning came, he ordered that the servant be sold and that I be removed from the house.

key_terms.أَبْوَابٍ مُغْلَقَةٍ: locked doors, emphasizing physical separation and concealment
key_terms.اتَّقُوا اللَّهَ: have taqwa of Allah; a command to act with God-consciousness
key_terms.خَادِمٌ: a servant attending within the household
key_terms.خَافُوا اللَّهَ: fear Allah; an admonition against sinful conduct
key_terms.نَبِيذٍ: nabidh, a fermented drink mentioned here as something sought before the act
key_terms.وَكِيلٌ: an appointed agent or representative serving on behalf of another

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith show the moral authority and awareness of Abū Muḥammad عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This report narrates an incident involving the agent of Abū Muḥammad عليه السلام, whose misconduct with a servant was exposed despite multiple locked doors separating them from the Imam عليه السلام. The narration highlights the Imam’s awareness, his moral admonition, and his decisive response to wrongdoing.

en.hubeali: Is’haq said, ‘Yahya Bin Al Qusheyri narrated to me from a town named as Qeyr saying,

‘There was an agent for Abu Muhammad<sup>asws</sup> (11<sup>th</sup> Imam<sup>asws</sup>) whom he<sup>asws</sup> had taken to be in a room of the house. There happened to be a white servant with him. So the agent intended the servant to himself, but he refused except if he comes to him with Nabeez (an intoxicating drink). So he brought the Nabeez for him and went over to him; and between him and Abu Muhammad<sup>asws</sup> there were three locked doors.

He (the narrator) said, ‘So the agent narrated to me saying, ‘I was paying attention to him when the doors opened up until he<sup>asws</sup> came in himself<sup>asws</sup> and paused at the door of the room, then said: ‘O you! Be pious to Allah<sup>azwj</sup> and fear Allah<sup>azwj</sup>!’. So when we were in the morning, he<sup>asws</sup> ordered to sell the servant and threw me out from the house’.
en.sarwar: 19. Ishaq has said that narrated to me Yahya ibn al-Qushayri from the town called Qir the following. “

Abu Muhammad (a.s.) had an agent who lived in a room in the house with white servant of the Imam (a.s.). the agent invited the servant to have evil activities with him and the servant refused to do so unless he brought him wine. The agent managed to find wine and take it to him. There were three closed doors between them and the quarters of the Imam (a.s.).

The narrator has said that the agent narrated to me that was awake and I saw the doors open until I saw the Imam (a.s.) in person standing at the door. He then said, “O you have fear of Allah and be pious before Him. In the morning he ordered to sell the servant and discharge me from the job.”
